H1.note: IL12B claims start from the chain's two variants (one claim each); IL23R enters the chain as the receptor node at H1.2, so its claim starts there. The protective IL23R variant rs11209026 that the mechanism leans on is in no step.

H2.note: NOD2 claims start from the chain's three risk alleles; the LACC1 chain starts at the protein (the title names LACC1 risk alleles, but no step does), and 'risk alleles blunt clearance' makes LACC1's own sign negative

H3.no_claim_reason: the run states that the direction of GPR35's effect on Crohn disease is unresolved (opposite knockout phenotypes, a protective and risk alleles), and the title and mechanism give no sign

findings.detail: Neither IL12B GWAS row says anything about p40 or IL-23 amount, and the run's own note admits the direction on p40 is inferred; the first link of the H1 chain has no support.
IL23R to Th17 commitment and IL-17 production is cited only to STRING over-representation results and an undirected MGI 'abnormal CD4 T cell differentiation' row.

Th17/IL-17 to Crohn disease is cited to a mouse Il23r colitis row, a ChEMBL row that ustekinumab is approved (no indication), and a recruiting tulisokibart trial with no results; none mentions Th17 or IL-17.

NCT06430801 is cited as validating the IL-23 axis, but the record names no target for tulisokibart; to the curator's knowledge (not in the text) tulisokibart is an anti-TL1A antibody, not an IL-12/IL-23 agent.

H1.3 ends at 'Th17 lineage commitment and IL-17 production', H1.4 starts at 'Th17/IL-17 mucosal response'; the IL-17 production parts join, but Th17 lineage commitment (GO:0072540) is not a Th17 immune response (GO:0072538), so the Th17 half does not connect.

rs11209026 (the protective IL23R coding variant the mechanism leans on), rs7517847, PMID:17068223, both OT association scores, CHEMBL3990029, STRING:GOCC:0072536 and the Treg CELLxGENE row support no step; no step starts from an IL23R variant.

OT:IL23R-safety is filed as contradicting (adenoma, paradoxical psoriasiform reactions), contradicts no step, and its copied UniProt function text is the only text the run saw that states H1.2 (IL23R binds IL-23 and mediates T-cell stimulation); it is excluded at H1.2 because the run did not offer it as support.
IL-23 activating IL23R is cited only to a CELLxGENE detection-rate row and a Reactome over-representation result; neither names IL-23 acting on the receptor.
Confidence 'high', but no H1 step has a text the run cited for it that states it; the therapeutic-validation argument rests on records that give neither indication nor efficacy.

CHEMBL:CHEMBL3990029 says 'RISANKIZUMAB targets IL12B'; to the curator's knowledge (not in the text) risankizumab binds IL-23 p19 (IL23A), so this looks like a complex-to-gene mapping artefact in the source; the run's mechanism ('p40/p19 blockade') is consistent with either.

H2.1 ends at NOD2 signalling and H2.2 starts at LACC1; no step links NOD2 signalling to cytokine output or bacterial clearance, so the three NOD2 alleles have no route to Crohn disease and the claimed NOD2-LACC1 convergence is never stated as a step.

H2.2 ends at cytokine secretion / bacterial clearance, H2.3 starts at the purine nucleotide cycle / OXPHOS and ends at macrophage activation, H2.4 starts at bacterial clearance; the only route (LACC1 to clearance to Crohn) skips H2.3 entirely.

PMID:11385576, which the run cites at H2.4, proposes that the NOD2 frameshift and missense variants act by over-activating NF-kB, the opposite of H2.1's 'inhibits'; it is a hypothesis in a 2001 genetics abstract, so it carries no weight, but the run did not engage with it.
No cited text says the NOD2 risk alleles reduce MDP-NOD2-RIPK2-NF-kB signalling: the GWAS rows are disease associations and UniProt Q9HC29 describes wild-type NOD2 with no variant.
H2.3 and H2.4 have no supporting text: the MGI rows are about the Lacc1 or Nod2 gene with undirected or off-target phenotypes, and PMID:11385576 does not mention bacterial clearance.

STRING:NOD2-LACC1 is cited as chain evidence, supporting and contradicting at once; it is a text-mining-only edge (experimental 0, database 0) and cannot back the 'physically associates' claim in the mechanism.

The title says risk alleles at both loci act through the module, but the LACC1 variants rs3764147 and rs1373904 (and PMID:27478939 on p.I254V/p.C284R loss of function) are in no step; the LACC1 half starts at the protein.
Confidence 'high', but the NOD2 half has no route to the disease and the LACC1 half rests on one UniProt sentence plus an unsupported H2.4.

OT:LACC1-tractability and CHEMBL:no-target-LACC1 are filed as contradicting, but the absence of drugs or tractability says nothing against a mechanism; the tractability record even repeats the supporting UniProt text.
AGR:MGI:1929509:MP:0013299 is cited as chain evidence at H3.4 and as contradicting, and OT:GPR35-MONDO_0005011 as both supporting and contradicting.

The only text for GPR35 to neutrophil recruitment and bacterial clearance is UniProt's 'plays a role in', which gives no direction; the other citation is an undirected MGI 'abnormal chemokine level' row.
HPA:ENSG00000178623 (an expression profile) is cited for ligand activation of GPR35; the step is carried by UniProt and PMID:40623474 instead.

PMID:40623474, cited at H3.1, reports that KYNA alleviated mesenteritis and colitis in two mouse models and acted via GPR35 signalling, which bears on the direction the run calls unresolved; the run used it only for ligand activation.

The abstention says CELLxGENE Crohn-vs-normal detection rates are a cross-study comparison and 'not a differential-expression result', yet H1, H2 and H3 cite the same kind of row as mechanistic support ('IL23R detection rises ~3-fold', 'GPR35 roughly doubled').

The GWAS rows for rs755374, rs2066844, rs2066845 and rs34236350 name no allele ('-?'), so 'risk allele' directions for these variants are fixed only by convention, not by the cited record; the rs34236350 association (S20) is therefore unsigned.
The rs2066847 GWAS row gives odds ratio 3.103 with interval [1.497-1.618], which excludes its own point estimate; the run took the row at face value.
rs2066845 and rs3749171 rows are for a five-disease pleiotropy trait (AS, CD, psoriasis, PSC, UC), not Crohn disease specifically, but are cited as Crohn support.
The MEIS1/TRIM4 abstention cites 14 accessions, none of which is in sources.json, so the abstention cannot be checked against text; its reasoning reads as sound.

No target form for the amount of a protein complex: GO:0070743 'interleukin-23 complex' is a GO component, which amount targets reject, so the IL-23 heterodimer is grounded as the process GO:0032627 'interleukin-23 production' (the run's increases_amount becomes a process target, and H1.2's subject is IL-23 production).
No GO process for 'bacterial clearance'; grounded to the parent GO:0042742 'defense response to bacterium', which is broader than the run's node.
terms.py finds CHEBI:27823 only by its systematic name '(5-hydroxyindol-3-yl)acetic acid'; '5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid' and '5-HIAA' return only HP/NCIT/VT terms.

Open Targets records (OT:LACC1-tractability, OT:GPR35-tractability, OT:IL23R-safety) copy UniProt function text, so one curated sentence can reach a run under two accessions; there is no dedup rule, and I excluded the copies as 'other' where the UniProt record was also cited.
No form for a step whose cited texts give opposite signs (two Gpr35 knockout alleles): it can only be 'no_sign', and the unexpressed entry's evidence cannot record which direction each text gives.
A hypothesis that honestly declines a direction gets no claim, so its four signed GWAS associations and its ligand steps never compose into anything; there is no 'test without a sign' form.
PMID:40623474's span does not say whether the GPR35 dependence came from the colitis mice or the cultured explants; recorded as mechanistic, mouse, because the same span reports disease course.

One curatedDb sentence gives belief 4/5 and verdict 'established' on its own: S11/S12 split one UniProt sentence into two established statements and S17 rests on one UniProt clause, while signed genome-wide GWAS rows (S21-S23, p down to 6e-19) stay at belief 1/2, 'unsupported'.

The guide does not say whether a populated run 'context' field limits a step; I dropped the CD4 T cell context at H1.2 (IL-23 activating IL23R is not specific to it) and refined bacterial clearance to macrophages at H2.2/H2.4, where the macrophage is the point of the hypothesis.
OT:NOD2-MONDO_0005011 and OT:LACC1-MONDO_0005011 (gene-level Open Targets scores, no direction) are supporting citations that bear on no step.
CHEMBL:target-CHEMBL1293267 only says ChEMBL has a target record for GPR35; it supports no step.

The mechanism says IL23R detection rises ~3-fold in colonic CD4 T cells, Tregs and CD8 T cells, but only the CD4 (7.6% vs 2.5%) and Treg (3.6% vs 1.0%) CELLxGENE rows are cited; the CD8 T cell figure has no source.

The mechanism says colonic macrophages show the highest LACC1 detection of any profiled cell type, but the run cites only the macrophage CELLxGENE row (17.3% vs 12.4%), so the comparison across cell types has no source.

For a GWAS row that names no allele ('rs34236350-?', beta increase), labelling the subject 'effect allele' and taking the row's direction is circular: some allele of any associated SNP raises risk. The guide should say such a row gives direction none.

The rs4676410 row comes from a sex-dimorphic IBD study run on women only (10,760 female cases, 22,345 female controls; p = 1e-8), but the run lists it as a general Crohn association; S23 states it unrestricted because a refinement has no sex field.

audit.after: il23 = GO:0032627 'interleukin-23 production' (process); S1/S2 target {process: il23}; missing_term finding removed, no_form_for finding reworded
audit.reason: the guide allows a BLN term only when nothing in any ontology fits. GO:0032627 is defined as the appearance of IL-23 'resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels', so it is the run's 'increases_amount of IL-23' (production of X = X at BioLean's grain, as with 'MUC5B expression'). It was the first hit for 'interleukin-23', which the curator searched but did not list. A BLN term can never match the same node in another run; the multi_agent-r2 Crohn curation grounds IL-23 as GO:0032627 too. Routes unchanged.

'The effect allele raises risk' is true by definition for any associated SNP, so it carries no direction for an identifiable allele. A dbSNP entity must name its allele. No arm changes (H3 has no claim).

the step's subject is 'GPR35 CD-associated variants', and the curator itself treats another GPR35 variant cited only as supporting (rs4676410) as a member. What fails is the trait: the row is for a five-disease pleiotropy trait (AS, CD, psoriasis, PSC, UC), a broader disease than Crohn.
